summary: The country dossier located no province-specific trans ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding for this division. Sejong is the administrative capital (government ministries relocated there), yet the dossier records no official-climate signal either way for trans people there. Its three sources are national-level: a Seoul court ruling on police restroom advice, an unrestored Yonhap wire, and a national school-restroom survey — none document Sejong-specific incidents.

sources.summary: Korea Times (22 Jul 2024): Seoul Central District Court ruled that a police officer advising a person in gender transition to avoid public restrooms for a while was a human-rights infringement, awarding 300,000 won of a 3 million won claim; the officer had received NHRCK human-rights education before the suit. National/Seoul-level — no Sejong content.
NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (navigation shell only; no article body preserved in cache); underlying Yonhap English wire, 8 May 2024, content not verifiable.

Hankyoreh (21 Mar 2024): a youth LGBTQ+ center surveyed 86 trans/genderqueer students — 69% did not feel comfortable using school restrooms, with students describing avoiding drinking to skip urination; a separate Busan study of 208 students found 39% mistreated at school over gender identity or sexual orientation. Advocacy targets the educational-facilities and school-health acts for gender-inclusive facilities. National-level — Sejong not covered.
